newsitem.title: JAPAN: Faulty motor to be changed at Japan Monju reactor.
newsitem.headline: Faulty motor to be changed at Japan Monju reactor.

text.p: The operators of Japan's prototype fast-breeder nuclear reactor said on Monday that it would change a motor for one of the pumps at the plant as it appeared to be malfunctioning.
The reactor, known as Monju, remains shut down after an accident in which an estimated two to three tonnes of liquid sodium leaked from a cooling system on December 8.

A spokesman for the operators, the state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp, said the temperature of the motor had been hitting 80 degrees Celsius, when the normal operating temperature was about 45 degrees Celsius.
The motor operates a pump which circulates sodium within the reactor.
"The pump will be stopped today and steps to exchange the motor will begin after that," the spokesman said.
He said the pump was not located near the area of December's accident, and was most probably unrelated to it.
An investigation into the cause of the accident -- which the operators say caused no damage to the environment -- is continuing.
